entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Theophylact was an archdeacon of the Roman Church, serving under Pope Stephen II and Pope Paul II, who was chosen as the successor after Stephen II's death in 757. Theophylact played a crucial role in the Synod of Frankfurt in 794, where he represented Pope Adrian I as one of his legates.

Theophylact's significance lies in his involvement in the papal service during a period of significant change in the Roman Church, particularly the succession crisis following Stephen II's death. His participation in the Synod of Frankfurt highlights the importance of the archdeacon's role in facilitating the papal authority during times of transition.

Theophylact's legacy is closely tied to the development of the papal service and the evolution of the Roman Church's leadership during the Late Antiquity and Early Middle Ages.

Theophylact's influence can be seen in the continuation of the papal service under subsequent popes, including Paul II and Adrian I, who relied on the expertise and loyalty of archdeacons like Theophylact to maintain the Church's authority and stability.
